{{nihongo|'''Kōra Taisha'''|高良大社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Chikugo Province]].

[[File:View from Kora Taisha Shrine.jpg|270px|thumb|View from the grounds of Kora Taisha Shrine]]'''Kora Taisha'' is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|abstract|Q845945|ar|جينجا|arz|ضريح شنتو|bcl|Shinto shrine|ca|Jinja|cs|Šintoistická svatyně|da|Shinto-tempel|de|Shintō-Schrein|el|Σιντοϊστικό Ιερό|eo|Ŝintoa sanktejo|es|Jinja|eu|Jinja|fa|معبد شینتویی|fi|Šintolainen pyhäkkö|fr|Sanctuaire shinto|hi|शिंतो मंदिर|hr|Šintoistički hram|hu|Sintó szentély|id|Jinja|it|Jinja|ja|神社|ka|ძინძია|ko|신사 (신토)|lb|Shintō-Schräin|mr|शिंतो मंदिर|nl|Jinja (heiligdom)|no|Jinja|or|ଜିଞ୍ଜା|pl|Jinja|pt|Templo xintoísta|ru|Дзиндзя|sc|Jinja|simple|Shinto shrine|sl|Šintoistično svetišče|sr|Шинтоистички храм|sv|Jinja|th|ศาลเจ้าชินโต|tok|tomo sewi pi nasin sewi Sinto|tr|Şinto tapınağı|uk|Святилище (синто)|uz|Dzindzya|vi|Thần xã|wuu|神社|zh|神社|zh_yue|神社|qid=Q845945}} located in {{ill|Mount Kōra|Q11672746|qid=Q11672746}} in {{ill|Fukuoka Prefecture|Q123258|qid=Q123258}}{{ill|Kurume|Q320934|qid=Q320934}}. {{ill|Shikinaisha|fr|Shikinaisha|zh|式內社|qid=Q134917286|lt=Shikinaisha}} ({{ill|Myōjin Taisha|fr|Myōjin Taisha|ja|名神大社|simple|Myōjin Taisha|zh|名神大社|qid=Q9610964}}), {{ill|Chikugo Province|Q864159|qid=Q864159}}{{ill|Ichinomiya|Q1656379|qid=Q1656379}}. {{ill|Q712534|lt=Old Shrine Ranking}} is {{ill|Q712534|lt=Old Shrine}} is {{ill|Government Shrine|qid=Government Shrine|lt=Modern Shrine Ranking System}}, and currently it is {{ill|Beppyo shrine|ja|別表神社|mr|बेप्प्यो तीर्थ|simple|Beppyo shrine|zh|別表神社|qid=Q10898274}} of {{ill|Association of Shinto Shrines|Q908077|qid=Q908077}}.

In ancient times, it was also called ``Kora Tamatare no Mikoto Shrine'' (Kora Tamatare no Mikoto Jinja) and ``Kora Tamatare no Miya'' (Kora Tamatare no Miya).

== Overview ==
{{ill|Kurume|Q320934|qid=Q320934}} It is located to the east of the center.

Regarded as the national soul of Tsukushi since ancient times, devout religious areas can be found not only in {{ill|Chikugo Province|Q864159|qid=Q864159|lt=Chikugo}}, but also in Hizen, mainly in areas near the Ariake Sea. It is also famous for its blessings on bad luck, warding off bad luck, prolonging life and traffic safety in modern times. He is also believed to be the god of entertainment.

Kora Taisha itself is a Meishin Taisha, a shrine in Chikugo Province, and the {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Toyohime Shrine}}, which is enshrined in the main shrine, is a Meishin Taisha, a subsidiary shrine outside the precincts, {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Ise Amaterasu Miso Shrine}} is a small shrine in Shikinai, and {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Ajisumi Shrine}} is Chikugo Province {{ill|Sōja shrine|Q1107129|qid=Q1107129}}.

The shrine building has been designated as a national important cultural property and is one of the largest shrine buildings in Kyushu.

== Enshrined God ==
* Seiden: ``Kora Tamatare no Mikoto'' - The divine crest is a ``horizontal melon'' and the divine messenger is a ``crow.''
* Left Hall: '''{{ill|Hachiman|Q261637|qid=Q261637|lt=Hachiman Okami}}''' (Hachiman Okami) - The divine crest is "right three tomoe" and the divine messenger is "dove"
* Right temple: '''{{ill|Sumiyoshi sanjin|Q1114013|qid=Q1114013|lt=Sumiyoshi Okami}}''' (Sumiyoshi Okami) - The divine crest is “57 paulownia,” and the divine messenger is “crane.”

In addition, there is a guest room inside the main shrine, where ``Toyohime Okami'' is enshrined. There is also a theory that Takara Tamatarumei were a married couple. The divine rank is {{ill|Senior Fourth Rank|ja|正四位|ko|정4위|zh|正四位|qid=Q11123338|lt=Senior Fourth Rank Lower}}. For details, see {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Toyohime Shrine}} below. Other deities enshrined in the shrine grounds include the deities of {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Sakamoto Shrine}}, which were located within the precincts.Takara Tamatare no Mikoto was given {{ill|Senior First Rank|Q11123258|qid=Q11123258}} by the Imperial Court, but he does not appear in the chronicles, and there has been a long-standing dispute as to who his real identity is. Ominori no Yasu, {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Tsuki Tenshi}}, incarnation of {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Sumiyoshi Myojin}}, distant ancestor of the Mononobe clan, {{ill|Mononobe no Ikui|Q55536819|qid=Q55536819|lt=Mononobe Ikukuren}}, Mononobe Horen) theory, {{ill|Mononobe clan|Q1755836|qid=Q1755836|lt=Mononobe}} ancestor god ({{ill|Nigihayahi|Q10949054|qid=Q10949054|lt=Nakushahi no Mikoto}}, Mononobe Ikuriren, Mononobe Horen) theory, {{ill|Hoori|abstract|Q1051960|bs|Hoori|fa|هوری (اسطوره ژاپن)|fr|Hoori|hr|Hoori|it|Hoori|ja|ホオリ|ko|호오리|mni|ꯍꯨꯔꯤ|nl|Ho-ori|no|Hoori|pl|Hoori|pt|Yamasatihiko|ru|Хоори|sh|Hoori|simple|Hoori|sr|Хоори|sv|Hoori|tr|Hoori|uk|Хоорі|vi|Hoori|zh|火折尊|qid=Q1051960|lt=Hikokademison}} theory, {{ill|Q1154888 5|qid=Q1154888 5|lt=Mizunuma-kun}} ancestor god theory, {{ill|Watatsumi|abstract|Q1474187|az|Vatatsumi|de|Watatsumi|es|Watatsumi|fa|واتاتسومی|fr|Watatsumi|hu|Vatacumi|ja|ワタツミ|ko|와타쓰미|mni|ꯋꯇꯠꯁꯨꯃꯤ|pl|Watatsumi|ru|Ватацуми|simple|Watatsumi|uk|Вататсумі|zh|綿津見|qid=Q1474187|lt=Watatsumi-kami}} theory, {{ill|Himekoso Shrine|Q11547445|qid=Q11547445|lt=Himeko Sojin}} ({{ill|Kawara Shrine (Q11667602)|Q11667602|qid=Q11667602|lt=Koshun}} same deity) theory, {{ill|Emperor Keikō|Q329723|qid=Q329723}} (Oashihiko) theory, {{j There are various theories such as the alink|Mana Serita}} theory, the {{ill|Silla|Q28456|qid=Q28456}} divine theory, and the {{ill|Goguryeo|Q28370|qid=Q28370|lt=Koryo}} divine theory. During the Edo period, the prevailing theory was that he was compared to Takeuchi Sukune, but since the Meiji period, no particular comparison has been made.

== History ==
{{ill|Emperor Nintoku|Q313119|qid=Q313119}} Enshrined in 1955 or 1978, {{ill|Emperor Richū|Q329704|qid=Q329704}} It is said to have been founded in 1997<ref>{{Cite book|Japanese book |title=Local cultural property |date=1982-3-31 |publisher=Kurume City Board of Education |page=4 |author=Kurume City Board of Education}}</ref>.

In the ``{{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|abstract|Q11064932|fr|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|simple|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|zh|延喜式神名帳|qid=Q11064932}}'', it is listed as ``{{ill|Chikugo Province|Q864159|qid=Q864159}}{{ill|Mii District, Fukuoka|Q1156095|qid=Q1156095}} Takaratamatarumei Shrine'' and is listed as a Meishin Taisha, as well as being considered as the Ichinomiya of Chikugo Province. Furthermore, according to the ``Chikugo-kuni Shinmyocho,'' which is said to be the oldest divine namebook in Japan, the enshrined deity Takara Tamatare-no-miko is said to have been awarded the rank of Shoichii by the imperial court.Originally, the deity {{ill|Takamimusubi|UNKNOWN|Takamimusubi|lt=Takagi|qid=Q125400}} (=Takamisuhi-kami, Takamure-kami) was enshrined in Mt. Takara, and it was called Takamure-yama. Legend has it that when Ryotatari no Mikoto asked to borrow the mountain for a night's lodging, Takagi no Kami gave it to him, and Tamatatari put up a {{ill|Bai sema|Q803695|qid=Q803695}} and was enshrined there. There is also a theory that the name of the mountain changed its sound from ``Takamure'' and came to be called ``Kora'' mountain by combining the two characters of the good character. Currently, Takagi-kami, the original guardian deity, is enshrined at {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Takagi Shrine}} in front of the second {{ill|Torii|ar|توري|az|Torii|bcl|Torii|bg|Тории|ca|Torii|cs|Torii|de|Torii|el|Τορίι|eo|Torijo|es|Torii|et|Torii|eu|Torii|fa|توریئی|fi|Torii|fr|Torii|he|טוריאי|hu|Torii|hy|Տորիի|id|Torii|it|Torii|ja|鳥居|jv|Torii|ko|도리이|lt|Torii|ms|Torii|nl|Torii|no|Torii|oc|Torii|pl|Torii|pt|Torii|ru|Тории|simple|Torii|sl|Tori|sq|Torii|sv|Torii|ta|தொரீ|th|โทริอิ|tr|Torii|uk|Торії|uz|Torii|vi|Torii|wuu|鳥居|zh|鳥居|qid=Q234731}} at the foot of the mountain. Furthermore, the name ``Takamutre'' remains in the name of the {{ill|Kurume City Hall|Q11369524|qid=Q11369524}} branch office in Kurume City {{ill|Mii|Q11488770|qid=Q11488770}}, ``Takamutre Civic Center,'' as well as in the names of several elementary and junior high schools in Kurume City and in the lyrics of their school songs.

== Setsusha, concurrent company, etc. ==
In addition to the following, Hosshin Gongen (Hosshin Sansha Daigongen) is listed as a subsidiary shrine in the Tamatare Palace Hinden and Precincts Sueshaki. </ref>. The old name of the enshrined place has been used to make it easier to understand.

Also called ``Suisisha.'' The former "Koryuji Bishamon-do" was renamed in the {{ill|Meiji era|Q3125096|qid=Q3125096}} {{ill|Shinto and Buddhism|qid=Shinto and Buddhism|lt=separation of Buddhism}}.

== Precincts ==
The inner part of the precincts is the third torii gate, Honzaka slope, and the downhill slope (Gekozaka) torii gate and stone steps. The current main approach to the shrine is Honzaka, but it is said that it used to be a downhill stone staircase.

=== Toyohime Shrine ===
; Toyohime Shrine
: {{ill|Shikinaisha|fr|Shikinaisha|zh|式內社|qid=Q134917286|lt=Shikiuchi Shrine}} ({{ill|Myōjin Taisha|fr|Myōjin Taisha|ja|名神大社|simple|Myōjin Taisha|zh|名神大社|qid=Q9610964|lt=Meishin Taisha}}). Old {{ill|Q712534|lt=Prefectural company}}. Currently, it is enshrined in the main shrine as {{ill|Setsumatsusha|es|Setsumatsusha|fr|Setsumatsusha|ja|摂末社|zh|攝末社|qid=Q1071160|lt=Setsusha}}. Enshrined deity: Toyohime Okami ({{ill|Toyotama-hime|de|Toyotama-hime|es|Toyotama-hime|fa|تویوتاما-هیمه|fi|Otohime|fr|Otohime|id|Toyotama-hime|ja|トヨタマヒメ|ko|도요타마히메|mni|ꯇꯣꯌꯣꯇꯃ-ꯍꯤꯃꯦ|pl|Toyotama-hime|ru|Тоётама-химэ|simple|Toyotama-hime|sv|Otohime|uk|Тойотама-хіме|vi|Toyotama-hime|zh|豐玉毘賣命|qid=Q2329261|lt=Toyota Hime no Mikoto}}).
: One of the essays of Meishin Taisha. {{ill|List of Shikinaisha in Chikugo Province|fr|Shikinaisha|zh|式內社|qid=Q134917286|lt=Shikiuchi Shrines in Mitsui District, Chikugo Province}} It is thought that the three troupes (two large and one small) were located in the same place, {{ill|Ten'an|Q1075611|qid=Q1075611|lt=Ten'an}} When the main building of Toyohime Shrine was burnt down in May of the first year of the year ({{ill|857|Q30374|qid=Q30374}}), there is a record that Takara Tadamaku Shrine was also damaged, so there is also a theory that it was in the side hall or in a close distance <ref name="picture" />. {{ill|Jōgan|Q1075635|qid=Q1075635|lt=Jogan}}On March 22, 11 ({{ill|869|Q23917|qid=Q23917}}), he was promoted to the upper rank of Shoshii. There is also a mention in the "Chikugo Province Shinmyocho," but after that it declined and became unknown. Therefore, there are multiple Ronshas.It is said that it was rebuilt as a subsidiary shrine in {{ill|Jōkyō|Q1146221|qid=Q1146221}} 2nd year ({{ill|1685|Q7660|qid=Q7660}}), but its main building is used as that of Maneko Shrine.<ref name="information board" /> Around the time of the {{ill|Meiji Restoration|Q8707|qid=Q8707}}, a small shrine of Toyohime Shrine was built and revived in the precincts of ``Shin-Shimizu Kannon-do'' on the summit of Mt. === Precincts Setsuesha ===
; City {{ill|Ebisu Shrine|Q11261031|qid=Q11261031|lt=Ebisu Shrine}} (Ichiebisusha) <ref name="Information board" /><ref name="Precincts">{{Cite web|Japanese book|url=http://www.kourataisya.or.jp/keidai/keidai01 |title=Information about the precincts |website=Kora Taisha Shrine |accessdate=2018-05-30}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |Japanese book |title=Faith of Mt. Kora (6) Ebisu-san |date=2013-10-01 |publisher=Kora Taisha Shrine Office |journal=Tamatare |issue=26 |page=6 |url=http://www.kourataisya.or.jp/wp/wp-content/uploads/2013/05/tamatare26.pdf }}</ref>
: Precinct company. Deity enshrined: Couple {{ill|Ebisu (mythology)|Q1129330|qid=Q1129330|lt=Ebisu God}}. Annual Festival (Ebisu Grand Festival): {{ill|September 25|Q2886|qid=Q2886}}.
: A shrine in {{ill|Marketplace|Q330284|qid=Q330284|lt=city}} that was originally enshrined in Fuchu, Miimachi, at the foot of the mountain. It is said that when a market was held near Chikugo Province, it was customary to obtain permission from the Mt. Takara Festival and to pray for the god Ebisu. There are still several stone statues of Ebisu in Fuchu-juku and Shimomiya.
; {{ill|Inna Shrine|Q11409128|qid=Q11409128}} (Innyaku Jinja) <ref name="information board" /><ref name="precincts" />: Precincts end shrine. Enshrined deity: Takeuchi Sukune. Regular festival: November 13th (Sessuesha regular festival).
: Also called ``Inkasha.'' In 1873 (Meiji 6), it was solicited from {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Inka Shrine}} in Munesaki, Miimachi, which will be mentioned later. In the ``Kokuhei Chusha Takara Shrine Ezu'' dated around the middle of the Meiji period, the enshrined deity is said to be ``Inka of Takara Shrine.''<ref name="Ezu" />
; Kora Miko Shrine <ref name="Information board" /><ref name="Precincts" />
: Precinct Setsusha. Regular festival: November 13th (Sessuesha regular festival), Monthly festival: 13th of every month.
:* Deities enshrined: 9 Mikogami of Takara Tamadaumei, 9 Princes
:** First Prince Shiregashi no Mikoto
:** Second Prince Asahi Yosakari no Mikoto
:** Third Prince Kurehito Yosakari no Mikoto
:** Fourth Prince Fuchishino Mikoto
:** Fifth Prince Tanigami no Mikoto
:** Sixth Prince Naomi Mikoto
:** Seventh Prince Sakamoto Mikoto
:** Eighth Prince Ashiki Mikoto
:** Ninth Prince Anraku Ohobi no Mikoto.
: Also called ``Kora Mikosha.'' In 1873 (Meiji 6), it was solicited from {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Kora Miko Shrine}} located in Ojiyama, Yamakawa Town, which will be mentioned later.
; Maneko Shrine <ref name="Information board" /><ref name="Picture" /><ref name="Precincts" />: Precincts end shrine. Enshrined deity: {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Maneko Iki}}. Regular festival: November 13th (Sessuesha regular festival).
: Also called ``Manekosha.'' {{ill|1935|Q18658|qid=Q18658}} (Showa 10), Gosho Hachiman Shrine, Hiyoshi Shrine, and Fuunami Shrine, which were also within the precincts, were enshrined together. The current shrine building is said to be the former shrine building of {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Toyohime Shrine}}, which was rebuilt in 1685.
:; {{ill|Gosho Hachimangu Shrine|Q11372384|qid=Q11372384}}

:; {{ill|Furogu Shrine|Q11282543|qid=Q11282543|lt=Furou Shrine}}
:: Precincts end shrine. Enshrined deity: {{ill|Watatsumi|abstract|Q1474187|az|Vatatsumi|de|Watatsumi|es|Watatsumi|fa|واتاتسومی|fr|Watatsumi|hu|Vatacumi|ja|ワタツミ|ko|와타쓰미|mni|ꯋꯇꯠꯁꯨꯃꯤ|pl|Watatsumi|ru|Ватацуми|simple|Watatsumi|uk|Вататсумі|zh|綿津見|qid=Q1474187|lt=Watatsumi}}.:: In ancient times, it was called ``Furōgongen''<ref name="Sueshaki" />``Furōsha''<ref name="Pictures" />.

== Yamauchi ==
It branches off from the road (Fukuoka Prefectural Route 750) at the second torii gate. At the top of the approach, it merges with a temporary bus-only road that separates from the road near the Shimo-mukazaka torii gate, and further on, near the San-no-Torii gate, where it merges with the road.

=== Along the Yamauchi approach ===
; Kagamiyama Shrine <ref name="picture" />
: Outside the precincts. Enshrined deity: The branch ancestor of Takara Tadamari no Mikoto. Regular festival: November 13th (Sessuesha regular festival).
: It was originally enshrined in Karawa, Miimachi, at the foot of the mountain, but due to the construction of the {{ill|Kyushu Expressway|Q1060803|qid=Q1060803}}, it was moved to its current location, the site of the middle temple of Mt. Takara. It enshrined the Four Clouds Bunjukenkyokyo mirror housed in the Kora Taisha Treasure Museum.
; Ise Amaterasu Mioyajinja Shrine<ref name="Yamauchi" /><ref name="Information board" />
: Outside the precincts. Shikinaisha (small). Enshrined deity: {{ill|Amaterasu|Q455602|qid=Q455602}}. Regular festival: November 13th (Sessuesha regular festival).
: Enshrined in Nakatani, Miimachi. It is also called ``Ise Goso Shrine''. In ancient times, it was called ``Ise Shrine,'' ``Oso Shrine'' and ``Isemioya.'' In {{ill|Enryaku|Q1373176|qid=Q1373176}} 3rd year ({{ill|784|Q30083|qid=Q30083}}), it was enshrined separately from {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|Q11581011|qid=Q11581011}} in Ise. In the "Korasha Picture Engi" written at the end of the {{ill|Muromachi period|Q334845|qid=Q334845}}, a small shrine is depicted north of the stone Otorii gate (currently the main gate of Mii Elementary School, near the Fuchu-juku Honjin site "Isenoi"). However, due to the Fuchu Great Fire in {{ill|Meiwa|Q1146161|qid=Q1146161}}4 ({{ill|1767|Q7672|qid=Q7672}}), it was relocated to its current location.: Same as {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Ise Amaterasu Miso Shrine}} in Oishi-cho, Kurume City, it is a small Shikinai Ronsha shrine, but the deity enshrined is different.
:; {{ill|Hachiman shrine|Q11390939|qid=Q11390939}} (Hachimanguu) <ref name="information board" />
:: Outside the precincts. Enshrined within the grounds of Ise Amaterasu Miso Shrine.
:: It was originally located somewhere else in the mountain, but due to maintenance, it was moved to the grounds of Ise Amaterasu Miso Shrine. ``Wakamiya Hachiman Shrine'' is listed as a subsidiary shrine in the ``Tamataruregu Hinden and Precincts Sueshaki'', but since there are multiple Hachiman shrines around Mt. Takara, it is unclear whether this refers to our company <ref name="Susushaki" />.
:; {{ill|Tenmangū|Q798838|qid=Q798838}} (Tenmanguu)<ref name="information board" />
:: Outside the precincts. Enshrined within the grounds of Ise Amaterasu Miso Shrine.
:: It was originally located somewhere else in the mountain, but due to maintenance, it was moved to the grounds of Ise Amaterasu Miso Shrine. ``Tamataregu Hinden and Precincts Sueshaki'' lists ``Tenmangu'' as a subsidiary shrine, but since there are multiple Tenman Shrines around Mt. Takara, it is unclear whether this refers to our company.; Dai{{ill|Benzaiten|lt=Benzaiten|Q818468|qid=Q818468|qid=Q818468|lt=Benzaitensha}} (Daibenzaitensha)<ref name="Benten-sama">{{Cite journal |Japanese book |title=Faith in Mt. Kora (Eleventh) Benten-sama |date=2016-10-01 |publisher=Kora Taisha Shrine Office |journal=Tamatare |issue=35 |page=5 |url=http://www.kourataisya.or.jp/wp/wp-content/uploads/2013/05/%E3%81%9F%E3%81%BE%E3%81%9F%E3%82%8C35%E5%8F%B7-ilovepdf-compressed-min-1-1.pdf }}</ref>
: Kyougaisha. A stone pagoda sits in the bamboo thicket just after entering the second torii gate. On the back side, it says "White Snake Mound".

=== Along Yamauchi Road ===
; Daigaku Inari Shrine <ref name="Yamauchi" /><ref>{{Cite journal |Japanese book |title=240 years since the enshrinement of Daigaku Inari Shrine |date=2011-06-01 |publisher=Kora Taisha Office |journal=Tamatare |issue=19 |page=5 |url=http://www.kourataisya.or.jp/wp/wp-content/uploads/2013/05/tamatare19.pdf }}</ref>

Inari in Munesaki, Miimachi. "{{ill|Inari shrine|Q514480|qid=Q514480}}"<ref name="picture" />In addition to being called "Inari Shrine," it was also called "Atagoyama Inari" in ancient times. It is one of the largest shrines among the final shrines of Kora Taisha Shrine, said to be the first of the ten Chikuzen and Chikugo Inari shrines, and was commissioned from {{ill|Fushimi Inari-taisha|Q714828|qid=Q714828}} in Kyoto to the precincts of Atago Shrine in 8th year of the Meiwa era ({{ill|1771|Q7686|qid=Q7686}}). The current site was opened in {{ill|Keiō|Q776775|qid=Q776775}} 2nd year ({{ill|1886|Q7822|qid=Q7822}}) and relocated in {{ill|1875|ab|1875|af|1875|als|1875|am|1875 እ.ኤ.አ.|an|1875|ar|1875|ary|1875|arz|1875|ast|1875|av|1875 сон|avk|1875|az|1875|azb|۱۸۷۵ (میلادی)|ba|1875 йыл|ban|1875|bar|1875|bat_smg|1875|bcl|1875|be|1875|be_x_old|1875|bg|1875|bn|১৮৭৫|bpy|মারি ১৮৭৫|br|1875|bs|1875.|ca|1875|cdo|1875 nièng|ce|1875 шо|ceb|1875|ckb|١٨٧٥|crh|1875|cs|1875|csb|1875|cv|1875|cy|1875|da|1875|de|1875|diq|1875|el|1875|eml|1875|eo|1875|es|1875|et|1875|eu|1875|fa|۱۸۷۵|fi|1875|fiu_vro|1875|fo|1875|fr|1875|frp|1875|frr|1875|fur|1875|fy|1875|ga|1875|gan|1875年|gcr|1875|gd|1875|gl|1875|gn|1875|gv|1875|hak|1875-ngièn|he|1875|hi|१८७५|hif|1875|hr|1875.|hsb|1875|ht|1875 (almanak gregoryen)|hu|1875|hy|1875|hyw|1875 թուական|ia|1875|id|1875|ilo|1875|io|1875|is|1875|it|1875|ja|1875年|jv|1875|ka|1875|kaa|1875|kk|1875 жыл|ko|1875년|krc|1875 джыл|ksh|Joohr 1875|ku|1875|kv|1875-ӧд во|la|1875|lb|1875|lez|1875 йис|li|1875|lij|1875|lld|1875|lmo|1875|lt|1875 m.|lv|1875. gads|mai|१८७५|map_bms|1875|mdf|1875|mg|1875|mhr|1875|mi|1875|min|1875|mk|1875|ml|1875|mn|1875 он|mr|इ.स. १८७५|mrj|1875 и|ms|1875|my|၁၈၇၅|myv|1875 ие|mzn|۱۸۷۵|nah|1875|nap|1875|nds|1875|new|सन् १८७५|nl|1875|nn|1875|no|1875|nov|1875|nrm|1875|nso|1875|oc|1875|olo|1875|or|୧୮୭୫|os|1875-æм аз|pa|1875|pl|1875|pnb|1875|pt|1875|qu|1875|ro|1875|ru|1875 год|rue|1875|sa|१८७५|sah|1875|scn|1875|sd|1875ع|se|1875|sh|1875.|shn|1875|si|1875|simple|1875|sk|1875|sl|1875|smn|1875|sq|1875|sr|1875|stq|1875|su|1875|sv|1875|sw|1875|szl|1875|ta|1875|te|1875|tg|Соли 1875|th|พ.ศ. 2418|tk|1875|tl|1875|tly|1875|tr|1875|tt|1875 ел|udm|1875 ар|uk|1875|ur|1875ء|uz|1875|vec|1875|vi|1875|vls|1875|vo|1875|wa|1875|war|1875|wuu|1875年|xmf|1875|yi|1875|za|1875 nienz|zea|1875|zh|1875年|zh_classical|一八七五年|zh_min_nan|1875 nî|zh_yue|1875年|qid=Q7764}} (Meiji 8th year). It is divided into Kami-sha (commonly known as Daigaku Inari-sha) and Shimo-sha (commonly known as Shogaku Inari-sha), and there are many Inari-sha shrines such as Sankuro Inari-sha and Sanshiro Inari-sha. Shimosha is said to have existed in this area even before Atago Shrine was built.
; {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Inyaku Shrine}} (Inyaku Shrine) |url=http://www.kourataisya.or.jp/wp/wp-content/uploads/2013/05/tamatare28.pdf }}</ref>: Former Sakaigai Suesha and later Kanemusha. Old {{ill|Q712534|lt=Village company}} Enshrined deity: Takeuchi Sukune, {{ill|Sugawara no Michizane|Q382005|qid=Q382005}}. Summer Festival: {{ill|July 17|Q2729|qid=Q2729}}, Winter Festival: {{ill|December 18|Q2438|qid=Q2438}}.: Enshrined in Munesaki, Miimachi. Enshrined in {{ill|Hakuhō|Q11580612|qid=Q11580612}}16 years ({{ill|676|Q31098|qid=Q31098}}). The place was originally the residence of the Grand Priest Munesaki, but in {{ill|Keichō|ca|Keichō|es|Keichō|fa|کیچو (دوره)|fr|Ère Keichō|id|Keichō|it|Keichō|ja|慶長|ko|게이초|ru|Кэйтё|simple|Keichō|sr|Кеичо|sv|Keichō|th|เคโช|tr|Keichō|uk|Кейтьо|zh|慶長|qid=Q1328185}} 6th year ({{ill|1601|Q6725|qid=Q6725}}), Munesaki Village was removed from the sacred territory of Kora Taisha Shrine and the shrine area was also included in Munesaki, so it became the {{ill|Ujigami|Q767655|qid=Q767655}} of Munesaki Village. In the ``Tamataregu Hinden and Precincts Sueshaki'', ``Inka Daimyojin'' is listed as a subsidiary shrine <ref name="Susyaki" />. In {{ill|Bunka|ca|Bunka|de|Bunka (Ära)|es|Bunka|fa|بونکا|fr|Ère Bunka|ia|Bunka|ja|文化 (元号)|ko|분카|ms|Zaman Bunka|ru|Бунка|simple|Bunka|sr|Бунка|sv|Bunka|tr|Bunka|zh|文化 (年號)|qid=Q1373146|lt=Bunka}}8 ({{ill|1811|Q6928|qid=Q6928}}), Lord Michizane Sugawara was enshrined. In 1873 (Meiji 6) {{ill|March 14|Q2404|qid=Q2404}} Gosha, {{ill|1921|Q2162|qid=Q2162}} ({{ill|Taishō era|Q329174|qid=Q329174}}10) {{ill|April 7|Q2505|qid=Q2505}} It is listed in Shinsensha. Inkan refers to the seal and key of Kora Taisha Shrine, and is said to be the key to protecting the treasure of Kora Taisha Shrine, or the shrine that protects Kora Taisha Shrine itself. Click here to visit {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Inna Shrine}} located within the grounds of Kora Taisha Shrine.
; Miyajidake Shrine <ref name="Yamauchi" />
: Outside the precincts. Enshrined deity: {{ill|Empress Jingū|Q232803|qid=Q232803}}. Regular festival: November 13th (Sessuesha regular festival).
: Enshrined at the top of Mt. Kokuzo, Mt. Rekiyama, Miimachi. A solicitation from {{ill|Miyajidake Shrine|Q3317296|qid=Q3317296}} in Fukutsu City, Fukuoka Prefecture.; Toseirei Shrine (Tosei Reishin no Yashiro, Tosei Reijinja)
: Outside the precincts. Enshrined deity: {{ill|Matsuo Bashō|Q5676|qid=Q5676}}.
: Enshrined within the grounds of Miyajidake Shrine. Built in February of {{ill|Kansei|Q1195131|qid=Q1195131}}8 ({{ill|1796|Q7818|qid=Q7818}}). It is said to be the first shrine in Japan to enshrine Matsuo Basho. It was originally located within the grounds of {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Toyohime Shrine}} after Shin-Shimizu Kannon-do on Mt. Shimizu, but due to the closure of Toyohime Shrine, the shrine site became part of the site of ``Suimeiso'', so {{ From jalink|1960|Q3754}} (Showa 35) to {{ill|1965|Q2650|qid=Q2650}} (Showa 40), it was relocated to the grounds of Miyajidake Shrine in Kokuzozan. The Jitoku Shrine of Shin-Shimizu Kannon-do has also been moved here.
Atago Shrine |url=http://www.kourataisya.or.jp/wp/wp-content/uploads/2013/05/tamatare34.pdf }}</ref>
: Outside the precincts. Enshrined deity: {{ill|Kagu-tsuchi|az|Kaqutsuçi|de|Kagutsuchi|es|Kagutsuchi|fa|کاگو-تسوچی|fr|Kagutsuchi|it|Kagutsuchi|ja|カグツチ|mni|ꯀꯒꯨ-ꯁꯨꯆꯤ|pl|Kagutsuchi|ru|Кагуцути|sv|Kagutsuchi|ta|ககுட்சூசி|tr|Kagutsuchi|uk|Кагу-цуті|zh|迦具土|qid=Q1640658|lt=Hikagu Earth God}}. Summer Festival: {{ill|July 23|Q2722|qid=Q2722}}, Monthly Festival: 4th of every month.: Miimachi Aza Rekiyama, enshrined at the top of Rekiyama. {{ill|Manji (era)|Q1145295|qid=Q1145295}} In 11 ({{ill|1660|Q7001|qid=Q7001}}), Kumayama (currently {{ill|Kurume University|de|Universität Kurume|es|Universidad de Kurume|ja|久留米大学|ko|구루메 대학|uz|Kurume universiteti|zh|久留米大學|qid=Q8191850}} Mii Gakusha), but because it was too far away to interfere with festivals, it was enshrined at its current location in {{ill|Kanbun (era)|Q1146228|qid=Q1146228}}11 ({{ill|1671|Q7610|qid=Q7610}}). In ancient times, it was called ``Atago Gongen.'' Commonly known as "Atago-san."
: There is Iwafudo in the precincts. Officially, it is a city-designated cultural property called ``Sanzon Magai Seeds,'' and the three seeds (Sanskrit characters) of Jizo Bodhisattva in the center and Fudo and Bishamon on the left and right sides are carved. The Seisando used to be next to the Iwafudo Sando, but it is not connected to the Ichi-no-Torii gate because it is blocked by the Kyushu Expressway.
: Nearby is Rekiyama Tumulus, and between Kora Shimomiya Shrine is {{ill|Gionyama Kofun|Q55527878|qid=Q55527878}}.

: Yoshimi-dake, Miimachi, enshrined at the summit of Mt. Yoshimi-dake. It is also called ``Kotohirasha''. On March 10, {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Yasunaga}}3 ({{ill|1774|Q7697|qid=Q7697}}), he was solicited from {{ill|Kotohira-gū|abstract|Q94760|az|Kotohira məbədi|de|Kotohira-gū|eu|Kotohira-gū|fr|Kotohira-gū|ja|金刀比羅宮|ko|고토히라궁|simple|Kotohira-gū|sl|Kotohira-gu|tr|Kotohira-gū|zh|金刀比羅宮|qid=Q94760}} in Sanuki. {{ill|Meiji – year 4|Q11512280|qid=Q11512280}} ({{ill|1871|Q7746|qid=Q7746}}), like the headquarters in Sanuki, Emperor Sutoku was enshrined here and the name was changed to ``Shirahosha'' and then ``{{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Kotohira Shrine}}.'' The ruins of Yoshimidake Castle are located in the same area.; {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Kora Miko Shrine}} (Kora Miko Shrine) <ref>{{Cite journal |Japanese book |title=Kanmatsusha Introduction Kora Miko Shrine |date=2011-10-01 |publisher=Kora Taisha Shrine Office |journal=Tamatare |issue=20 |page=6 |url=http://www.kourataisya.or.jp/wp/wp-content/uploads/2013/05/tamatare20.pdf }}</ref>
: Former Sakaigai Suesha and later Kanemusha. Deities enshrined: Nine deities and nine princes of Takara Tamatare no Mikoto (Shiregashi no Mikoto, Asahi Toyomori no Mikoto, Kurashi Toyomori no Mikoto, Fuchishi no Mikoto, Kyojo no Mikoto, Naonomi no Mikoto, Sakamoto no Mikoto, Anshiki no Mikoto, Anraku Oho no Mikoto).
: Enshrined in Ojiyama, Yamakawa Town. In ancient times, he was called ``Ashiki Oji'' and ``Kutai Oji''. Commonly known as "King's womb". Built on Mt. Ashiki during the {{ill|Emperor Ingyō|Q349258|qid=Q349258}} era. Moved to the current location in {{ill|Jingo-keiun|Q1373049|qid=Q1373049}}2nd year ({{ill|768|Q29961|qid=Q29961}}). The first prince, Shirekashi-no-Mikoto, was given the rank of Junior Fourth Rank (Junior Fourth Rank, Upper Rank), and the second and subsequent princes were given the Junior Fifth Rank (Higher Rank) (``Chikugo Province Jinmyocho''). It used to be a separate shrine, but later became independent and became the guardian deity of Yamakawa-cho Honmura and the general guardian deity of Yamakawa-cho. In ``Tamataregu Hinden and Precincts Sueshaki,'' ``Ousei'' is listed as a subsidiary shrine. Click here to visit {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=#Kora Miko Shrine}} located within the precincts of Kora Taisha Shrine.: Shrines within the precincts include Oji Wakamiya Hachimangu Shrine ({{ill|Emperor Nintoku|Q313119|qid=Q313119}}), Taijingu Shrine (Amaterasu Omikami), Ebisu Shrine, and Tenma Shrine (Sugawara Shrine (main village deity)). The "Fireworks Disturbance Bee" at Oji Pond is an annual festival of Wakamiya Hachiman Shrine, not Kora Miko Shrine ({{ill|September 15|Q2846|qid=Q2846}}). ``Wakamiya Hachiman Shrine'' is listed as a subsidiary shrine in the ``Tamataruregu Hinden and Precincts Sueshaki'', but since there are multiple Hachiman shrines around Mt. Takara, it is unclear whether this refers to our company <ref name="Susushaki" />.
:; Sakamoto Shrine (Sakamoto Shrine) <ref>{{Cite journal |Japanese book |title=Kanmatsusha Introduction Kuribayashi Sakamoto Shrine |date=2017-06-01 |publisher=Kora Taisha Shrine Office |journal=Tamatare |issue=37 |page=5 |url=http://www.kourataisya.or.jp/wp/wp-content/uploads/2013/05/%E3%81%9F%E3%81%BE%E3%81%9F%E3%82%8C37%E5%8F%B71.pdf }}</ref>
:: Former Sakaigai Suesha and later Kanematsusha. Regular festival: July 1st
::* Deity enshrined
::** Tosaka Head Office: Kushiiwa Madokami
::** Nishizaka Head Office: Toyoiwa Madokami:: Enshrined on the right side of the grounds of Takara Miko Shrine. The guardian deity of the entrance to Takarasando and the guardian deity of Kuribayashi, Yamakawa Town. It was enshrined at two locations, east and west, on the ancient road leading to Ashiki-zaka in Kuribayashi (near {{ill|Mii Station|Q4405132|qid=Q4405132}}). It was located at the north entrance, one of the three entrances to the ancient Mt. Takara (Mino Village, Ashiki Village, and Takarauchi Village), and the most important. ``Sakamoto Myojin'' is listed as a subsidiary shrine in the ``Tamataregu Guest Hall and Precincts Sueshaki'' <ref name="Susyaki" />. Part spirits were once enshrined on both sides of Honzaka in the precincts of Kora Taisha Shrine, but they have now been moved to the guest room inside the main shrine.

== Foothills ==
From the stone large torii (first torii) to the second torii.

; {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Takagi Shrine}} (Takagi Shrine) <ref name="information board" /><ref>{{Cite journal |Japanese book |title=Introduction to Kanematsusha Takaki Shrine |date=2012-06-01 |publisher=Kora Taisha Shrine Office |journal=Tamatare |issue=22 |page=4 |url=http://www.kourataisya.or.jp/wp/wp-content/uploads/2013/05/tamatare19.pdf }}</ref>
: Former Sakaigai Suesha and later Kanemusha. Old {{ill|Q712534|lt=Gosha}} (Shinsenheihakuryokushinsha). Enshrined deity: {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Takōsei Reishin}}. Annual festival: {{ill|December 13|Q2379|qid=Q2379}}.: Enshrined at Kamagoishi, Miimachi. In ancient times, it was called ``Takamure Gongen'' <ref name="Sushaki" /> ``Takamura Shrine'' <ref name="Illustrated map" />. As stated in {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=History}}, he is the landowner god of Mt. Kora, and was born in {{ill|Gangyō|Q747451|qid=Q747451}}2 years ({{ill|878|Q23910|qid=Q23910}}) Upper Junior Fifth Rank (``Nihon Sandai Jiroku''), and later ranked as {{ill|Senior Fifth Rank|Q11123280|qid=Q11123280|lt=Seigoi Lower}} (``Chikugo Province Shinmecho''). In 1873 (Meiji 6) {{ill|March 14|Q2404|qid=Q2404}} Gosha, {{ill|1922|ab|1922|af|1922|als|1922|am|1922 እ.ኤ.አ.|an|1922|ar|1922|ary|1922|arz|1922|ast|1922|av|1922|avk|1922|az|1922|azb|۱۹۲۲ (میلادی)|ba|1922 йыл|ban|1922|bar|1922|bat_smg|1922|bcl|1922|be|1922|be_x_old|1922|bg|1922|bh|1922|bn|১৯২২|bpy|মারি ১৯২২|br|1922|bs|1922.|bxr|1922 он|ca|1922|cdo|1922 nièng|ce|1922 шо|ceb|1922|ckb|١٩٢٢|co|1922|crh|1922|cs|1922|csb|1922|cv|1922|cy|1922|da|1922|de|1922|diq|1922|dsb|1922|el|1922|eml|1922|eo|1922|es|1922|et|1922|eu|1922|ext|1922|fa|۱۹۲۲|fi|1922|fiu_vro|1922|fo|1922|fr|1922|frp|1922|frr|1922|fur|1922|fy|1922|ga|1922|gag|1922|gan|1922年|gcr|1922|gd|1922|gl|1922|gn|1922|gv|1922|hak|1922-ngièn|he|1922|hi|१९२२|hif|1922|hr|1922.|hsb|1922|ht|1922 (almanak gregoryen)|hu|1922|hy|1922|hyw|1922 թուական|ia|1922|id|1922|ie|1922|ilo|1922|inh|1922 шу|io|1922|is|1922|it|1922|ja|1922年|jv|1922|ka|1922|kaa|1922|kbp|1922|kk|1922 жыл|kn|೧೯೨೨|ko|1922년|krc|1922 джыл|ksh|Joohr 1922|ku|1922|kv|1922-ӧд во|kw|1922|la|1922|lb|1922|lez|1922 йис|li|1922|lij|1922|lmo|1922|ln|1922|lt|1922 m.|lv|1922. gads|mai|१९२२|map_bms|1922|mdf|1922|mg|1922|mhr|1922|mi|1922|min|1922|mk|1922|ml|1922|mn|1922 он|mr|इ.स. १९२२|mrj|1922 и|ms|1922|my|၁၉၂၂|myv|1922 ие|mzn|۱۹۲۲|nah|1922|nap|1922|nds|1922|nds_nl|1922|nl|1922|nn|1922|no|1922|nov|1922|nrm|1922|nso|1922|oc|1922|olo|1922|or|୧୯୨୨|os|1922-æм аз|pa|1922|pam|1922|pap|1922|pl|1922|pnb|1922|pt|1922|qu|1922|ro|1922|roa_tara|1922|ru|1922 год|rue|1922|sah|1922 сыл|sc|1922|scn|1922|sco|1922|sd|1922ع|se|1922|sh|1922.|shn|1922|si|1922|simple|1922|sk|1922|sl|1922|smn|1922|sq|1922|sr|1922|stq|1922|su|1922|sv|1922|sw|1922|szl|1922|ta|1922|te|1922|tet|1922|tg|Соли 1922|th|พ.ศ. 2465|tk|1922|tl|1922|tly|1922|tpi|1922|tr|1922|tt|1922 ел|ty|1922|udm|1922 ар|ug|1922 - Mitarai Bridge, a stone bridge (designated by the prefecture as a tangible cultural property), was built in September 1803|Q6887}}.

== In town ==
Outside the stone large torii gate (first torii gate). There is a torii gate to the lower shrine next to the large stone torii gate.

The ``Kokuhei Chusha Kora Shrine Ezu'' dated around the middle of the Meiji period mentions ``Kyogaigōsha'' <ref name="Illustration" />.: In the shrine grounds, there are {{ill|Awashima Shrine (粟島神社)|Q11604588|qid=Q11604588}}, {{ill|Akiba Shrines|ja|秋葉神社|zh|秋葉神社|qid=Q11595841}}, Ebisu statue, {{ill|En no Gyōja|Q198946|qid=Q198946|lt=Engyoja}} statue (transferred from Gokurakuji Temple), Sarutahiko Okami, etc.
: There is a Gionyama kofun (tumulus) between Atago Shrine, and there is a theory that Soujin Shrine (Gion Shrine) was built to protect it. Even now, not only Sujin Shrine but also Kora Shimogu Shrine itself is sometimes commonly referred to as ``'''{{ill|Gion Faith|ja|祇園信仰|simple|Gion worship|qid=Q11588425|lt=Gion}}-san''''. In ``Tamataregu Hinden and Precincts Sueshaki,'' ``Shimomiya'' and ``Gion-sha'' are listed as separate shrines.
; Umashi Mizumi Shrine <ref name="Information board" /><ref name="Illustrated map" />
: Outside the precincts. Chikugo Province {{ill|Sōja shrine|Q1107129|qid=Q1107129}}. Enshrined deity: {{ill|Mizuhanome|it|Mizuhanome|ja|ミヅハノメ|pl|Mizuhanome|sv|Mizuhanome|zh|彌都波能賣神|qid=Q8191796|lt=Mizunami-no-mikoto}}. Regular festival: November 13th (Sessuesha regular festival). Summer Festival: {{ill|August 7|Q2781|qid=Q2781}}.: Miimachi Asazuma, located on the north side of {{ill|Kurume-Daigakumae Station|Q4405128|qid=Q4405128}}. In ancient times, it was called ``Asatsuma Shrine'' or ``Asazuma Daimyojin Shichiza.'' It is unknown when it was founded, but it is an old shrine that is listed as {{ill|Senior Sixth Rank|ja|正六位|ko|정6위|zh|正六位|qid=Q11545372|lt=Seniorokui Upper}} in the ``Chikugo Province Shinmecho'' written in {{ill|Tengyō|de|Tengyō|fa|تنگیو|fr|Ère Tengyō|ia|Tengyo|id|Tengyō|ja|天慶|ko|덴교|ru|Тэнгё|simple|Tengyō|sr|Тенгјо|tr|Tengyō|uk|Тенґьо (ненґо)|zh|天慶 (日本)|zh_yue|天慶 (日本)|qid=Q1327340}}7 ({{ill|944|Q24146|qid=Q24146}}). On the south side of Kurume University Station, there is a monument to the ruins of Kora Taisha Tungu Shrine (Tongu, or Setsusha), and the station was originally part of the shrine grounds. Asazuma Shimizu, one of the three springs of Takara and one of the top ten views of Mt. Takara, is the object of worship, and there is no torii gate or shrine building. After the 10th century, the Kokufu moved from Edamitsu, Aikawa Town to Asazuma, and it became Chikugo Kuni Soja. The sacred tree {{ill|Ilex rotunda|Q844306|qid=Q844306}} is a prefecturally designated natural monument.
: There is also a small shrine called ``Shichisha Gongen,'' which enshrines seven shrines (Asazuma Seven Shrines) that were previously enshrined separately in various parts of Asazuma. Amisumi Shrine does not have a shrine, so it is sometimes mistaken for this shrine. The deities enshrined are {{ill|Emperor Chūai|Q179971|qid=Q179971}}, Empress Jingu, Kuninaga Myojin, Kobo, {{ill|Myōken|Q10960623|qid=Q10960623|lt=Myoken}}, {{ill|Otomiya Shrine|Q11369923|qid=Q11369923|lt=Otomiya}}, {{ill|Nishinomiya Shrine|Q705297|qid=Q705297|lt=Nishinomiya}}.

== Other companies ==
There are a total of 16 shrines at the foot of Mt. Takara in the three precincts of Mii, Yamakawa, and Takara, including the aforementioned Inka Shrine, Takara Miko Shrine (Sakamoto Shrine), Takagi Shrine, and Takara Shimomiya Shrine. <ref>{{Cite journal |Japanese book |title=Concurrent shrine joint general meeting to be held at Mii precinct duty |date=2014-10-01 |publisher=Kora Taisha shrine office |journal=Tamatare |issue=29 |page=7 |url=http://www.kourataisya.or.jp/wp/wp-content/uploads/2013/05/tamatare291.pdf }}</ref>

== Related temples ==
;Koryuji Temple
: {{ill|Tiantai|Q668188|qid=Q668188}} temple. Abandoned temple. Until the middle of the Middle Ages, Takara Shrine ruled Takara Shrine as a shrine temple on Mt. Takara, but from the late Middle Ages onward it declined and was replaced by Miidera.
; Miidera
: Tendai sect temple. The name of the mountain is Mt. Takara, and the name of the temple is Rendai-in. Jinguji Temple on Mt. Kora from the late medieval period onwards. As the head of Mt. Kora, he ruled over 1,000 members of 360 temples and 26 temples. Due to the separation of Shinto and Buddhism ({{ill|Haibutsu kishaku|Q702298|qid=Q702298}}) in {{ill|Meiji – year 2|Q11512277|qid=Q11512277}} ({{ill|1869|Q7720|qid=Q7720}}), Buddhism was driven out of Mt. Kora, and all 26 temples of Mt. Kora were abandoned. The site of the main temple was used as the residence of the chief priest, and the site of the head priest was used as the Takarayama Palace. {{ill|1879|Q7783|qid=Q7783}} In April (Meiji 11), Miidera was rebuilt on the site of Hozoji Temple at the foot of the mountain.
; Mt. Kora 26 temples, Mt. Kora 12 temples
: There were many temples scattered along the approach to Kora Taisha Shrine, but as mentioned above, all of them have been abandoned.

== Local information ==

'''Location'''
* {{ill|Fukuoka Prefecture|Q123258|qid=Q123258}}{{ill|Kurume|Q320934|qid=Q320934}}1 Miimachi

'''Access'''

{{underline|Railway}}
* 9 minutes by taxi from {{ill|Kyushu Railway Company|Q498366|qid=Q498366|lt=JR Kyushu}}{{ill|Kyūdai Main Line|Q870569|qid=Q870569}} {{ill|Kurume-Daigakumae Station|Q4405128|qid=Q4405128}} (4.3km)

{{underline|bus}}
* From JR{{ill|Kurume Station|arz|محطة كوروم|fr|Gare de Kurume|it|Stazione di Kurume|ja|久留米駅|ko|구루메역|th|สถานีรถไฟคูรูเมะ|ur|کورومے اسٹیشن|zh|久留米站|qid=Q1122628}}/{{ill|Nishitetsu Kurume Station|Q7040736|qid=Q7040736}} direction, {{jalink|Nishitetsu Bus|Q11629843} } (via No. 1-1 Miimachi bound for {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Shiai Jogakuin}}), get off at the "Miimachi" bus stop, then take a taxi for 7 minutes or walk for 43 minutes (3.5km)
* During {{ill|Japanese New Year|ar|رأس السنة اليابانية|az|Yaponiyada Yeni il|bcl|Bagong Taon kan Hapon|bg|Японска нова година|ca|Cap d'any japonès|da|Japansk nytår|de|Japanisches Neujahrsfest|es|Año Nuevo japonés|eu|Japoniar urteberri-egun|fa|سال نوی ژاپنی|fr|Nouvel An japonais|hu|Japán újév|hy|Ամանորը Ճապոնիայում|id|Tahun baru Jepang|it|Capodanno giapponese|ja|正月|ko|쇼가쓰|mn|Японы шинэ жил|ms|Tahun Baru Jepun|pl|Shōgatsu|pt|Ano-novo japonês|ro|Anul Nou Japonez|ru|Новый год в Японии|simple|Japanese New Year|sr|Нова година у Јапану|ta|சப்பானியப் புத்தாண்டு|th|ตรุษญี่ปุ่น|tr|Japon Yeni Yılı|uk|Новий рік у Японії|uz|Yaponiyada yangi yil|vi|Tết Nhật Bản|zh|日本新年|qid=Q701398}} and festivals, there is a special bus from Nishitetsu Kurume Station to Kora Taisha Shrine.

{{underline|car}}* 4.7 km from {{ill|Kyushu Expressway|Q1060803|qid=Q1060803}}{{ill|Kurume interchange|Q1655312|qid=Q1655312}} via {{ill|Fukuoka Prefectural Road Route 750|ja|福岡県道750号御井諏訪野線|qid=Q11592822}} etc.
* Parking: Yes. By donating donations, you can ride the {{ill|Slope car|Q7541349|qid=Q7541349}} that makes it easier to visit the shrine from the parking lot.

'''Surroundings'''
* {{ill|Minō Mountains|arz|جبال مينو|ceb|Minō Sanchi|ja|耳納山地|lld|Ciadëina de Minō|qid=Q11610738}}
* {{ill|Mino Skyline|Q11610737|qid=Q11610737}}
* {{ill|Kōra-san Kōgoishi|Q46999756|qid=Q46999756}} (stone row remains)
** Yaba Stone Monument Remains - Located within the precincts. Yayo-ishi is the old name for Kamago-ishi, which is a ruined stone structure.
** Horseshoe Stone - Located near the second torii gate. This stone was originally called Kamago-ishi, and is said to be the origin of Yaba-ishi.
** Back comparison stone - Located near the second torii gate.
